steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Grease and flour a 9x13-inch baking pan.
Whisk vegetable oil, white sugar, eggs, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract together in a bowl until smooth.
Combine flour, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl.
Stir oil mixture into flour mixture until a well-mixed batter forms.
Fold carrots, pineapple, coconut, and walnuts into batter; pour into prepared baking pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 1 hour; cool completely, about 1 hour.
Whisk confectioners' sugar, cream cheese, butter, and a dash vanilla extract together in a bowl until well blended; spread over cooled cake.

raw_recipe.headline: Sister Beth's Carrot Cake
raw_recipe.description: This carrot cake combines carrots, pineapple, and cinnamon with shredded coconut and walnuts for a perfectly delicious cake. Homemade cream cheese frosting provides a smoothness with every bite.
raw_recipe.name: Sister Beth's Carrot Cake

review.reviewBody: Have used this recipe as is for years! Despite the other person saying to drain the pineapple, if you add the coconut do NOT drain it! This recipe is great as is-works great in an angel food pan too!

I made this two days ago. It is delicious and everyone really enjoyed it. I was so proud of the result.The pineapple is not noticeable as such in the baked cake, but really enhances the carrot/spice flavor. I will use this recipe every time in the future, it rocks!

Since I am not a fan of people changing the entire recipe and then rating their (very different) version of it, I only omitted the coconut (since I didn't have any) and used more carrot instead. I still had a few pecans and used those along with walnuts to make a whole cup (chopped in a food processor). Accidentally used less salt than the recipe stated, but it still came out really nice.

 I baked it for 48 minutes in a metal 9 by 13 inch pan lined with paper and it was done at that point, so checking after 45 minutes is important, I think (at sea level/no elevation). 

I recommend adding the pineapple last since the acid reacts with the baking soda to give the rise, and waiting too long before transferring the batter to the oven after mixing in the pineapple might affect the rise. I did drain the canned pineapple and then ran it through a food processor, since they don't sell crushed pineapple where I live. Even though there were a few minutes between mixing and baking in my case, it came out both fluffy and moist despite not much of a visible rise. I thought it might be wet or dense, but it was great!

I added a pinch of salt to the frosting because I think it enhances the vanilla flavor.

I drained the pineapple very well and think it could have used some of the juice. I also added a half cup of golden raisins and pecans instead of walnuts. Very good. I will make again with the modification. I made two round cakes for a layer cake and doubled the frosting recipe to put in between the layers.

After reading reviews I too decided to substitute 1 cup of applesauce for oil, and the cake turned out beautifully. I added a cup of raisins instead of using coconut. Borrowing from another recipe I also added grated orange zest to the frosting which gave it a nice flavour. Two thumbs up!

I’ve made this recipe twice and it was delicious both times. The first time I made it vegan using flax seed meal for the eggs and coconut sugar rather than white sugar. The second time, I followed the recipe. I also baked it in a 10” diameter round spring form pan. Have not tried the frosting yet. It’s so good that it does not need it.
first time making, family loved it. for the frosting though i only used 1/2 cup of conf. sugar and add 8oz of cream cheese, it was more cream cheesy tasting instead of too sweet.
I made these into cupcakes. Bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes. I also used 1 cup of sugar and 3/4 cup of honey instead of using 2 cup of sugar.

This is the first carrot cake I've made, and I don't need to keep looking! This cake is so delicious! I followed the recipe, omited nuts, baked in a glass 10x13 for 53 min and was glad I checked it when I did. It would have been dry if left for the full hour. The cake is moist, light, and so full of healthy fiber! I did end up doubling the frosting recipe. It didn't look like enough, and I really love cream cheese frosting ;)

Next time, I'll add more spices to get a spicier cake. I'd also like to try some golden raisins!
I cut the oil in half and added half cup apple sauce. very good !

This is almost identical to the recipe I have used for over forty years! The only difference was mine called for 1 1/2 cups of oil. I started using 3/4 cup of oil and 3/4 cup of applesauce and had good results. My recipe came from a Women's Club cookbook (early 70's). The recipe, if I remember correctly, was submitted by a home ec teacher. I had lost the recipe when I moved but luckily it was in a cookbook I had given my daughter. When I found this one I knew I could use it if my daughter didn't find it.
It was good, but I would recommend adding at least a tablespoon of cinnamon and some nutmeg or a pumpkin pie premixed spice.
I made this for my cousin and she said it was delicious.
It was amazing! I made it for my husband’s birthday he loved it! The only change I made was I used coconut oil instead of vegetable oil.
I can't say enough how much I LOVEEEEE this carrot cake recipe! It is fabulous. I don't change a thing.
Good cake. I omitted the coconut.
This is the absolute best carrot cake recipe i have found love it so easy to make ive made it 2x already
Added avocado and extract almond
Excellent and easy
Cake was good not too sweet, the frosting wasn’t as creamy
Followed the recipe exactly, except I added some extra chopped nuts on top for garnish. All in all, best carrot cake I've had in a long time!
